races.name: Bakers Tailoring Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Chesneys Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Ivan Furtado and Jason Hart with modest recent form (eighth in last two), but similar-going record is respectable at 1W2P from nine runs; the 1m2f trip on Good is fine but needs a stronger pace than Yafaarr is likely to set to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Chesneys Charm nevertheless catches the eye on a our rating of 77 — top of these, if only narrowly — and returns fit on just 14 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour from stall nine carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here; Sam England's four-year-old has shown real versatility in his role, winning over 8f on Good and placing four times, but carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he may race more prominently than ideally suited — that is less a concern here where he IS the pace and controls the race.
runners_data.comment: Yafaarr arrives in good heart after a second two starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and conditions and a rating edge over his official mark; the worry is a fourth last time out leaves something to prove.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's eight-year-old holds natural hold-up instincts but will find himself shuffled closer to the pace than he'd like given the density of rear-runners in this field; a consistent placer (0W2P on similar going) though winless in his last six, the combination of compromised position and advancing age makes this tough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Cosmos Raj nevertheless shows consistency in mid-division, with back-to-back fourths his most recent efforts; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 17 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, though 135 lb is a stern enough burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Always Blue
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's three-year-old is unexposed at 1m2f — her second at 10f at Goodwood is the key piece of form — and Sean Bowen is a meaningful booking; a natural hold-up type with limited similar-going data (2/4) but the trip extension profile is the most interesting angle in the race.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and close to her best, Always Blue has been placed twice in her last four starts and, rated 74, shapes as a leading threat from stall six over a trip and going she has experience of; the risk is that she remains winless in her last four outings.

runners_data.name: Boubyan
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse wearing a hood (hg:p), mapped forward only because the field is stacked with closers; recent form shows three consecutive placings on Good ground, and Lewis Edmunds rides, but finding a truly disadvantaged position undermines what is otherwise the most in-form closer in the field.
runners_data.comment: Boubyan has run over today's trip and going before and arrives fresh on a 16-day break, with consecutive thirds in his last two outings suggesting he is knocking hard on the door; yet to score in recent starts, the concern is whether he can convert that consistency into something more decisive from stall 8 off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Adiada
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' three-year-old runs with a hood (hg:h) and is lightly raced over this sort of trip; only one run on similar going from four recorded (0W0P) leaves plenty of uncertainty, and a 12-day turnaround with Rhys Elliott (5lb claim) suggests connections are keen — an unknown quantity in a race where position will be at a premium.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Adiada faces a stiff task here, though she shaped with promise when second three starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of 12 days from stall one carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has two wins at 10f on Soft or Standard from fifteen sim-going runs, suggesting the current Good ground is on the quick side of ideal; true hold-up style will be compromised by the crowded rear of the field, and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim only partially offsets the tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Sweet Kiss does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and a return in 12 days suggests she is ready, but a struggling trainer at 5% and a sixth-of-nine ranking make improvement hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ceinture d'Orion
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old is the one horse able to track Yafaarr comfortably and race to its natural prominent position; David Nolan's experience is an asset in a race where timing the challenge from second is the obvious route to victory, and three placings from five runs at 10f on Good are directly relevant form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Ceinture d'Orion faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 12-day turnaround showing the yard has her fit.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Pete
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's five-year-old has the lowest OR in the field (57) and, despite a second over 10f on Good in his history, recent form shows a string of poor finishes; Alex Jary's 3lb claim helps minimally, and as a true closer forced closer to the pace in a slow-run race, this looks a very difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with three unplaced efforts among recent outings, Whiskey Pete is hard to fancy from stall seven carrying 129 lb, though the runner-up finish last time and experience over today's distance and going offer slim encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Yafaarr is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 1m2f handicap at Redcar, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, Cian Horgan can dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable tempo on Good ground. Ceinture d'Orion is the only other runner with a prominent profile and should track Yafaarr into second, but the bulk of this field — Chesneys Charm, Always Blue, Cosmos Raj, Boubyan, Adiada, Sweet Kiss, and Whiskey Pete — are all hold-up types, meaning the early gallop is unlikely to be strong enough to stretch the field or cause carnage up front. The majority of the hold-up brigade have been redistributed in the map because there is simply insufficient room at the rear for all of them; Cosmos Raj, Boubyan, Sweet Kiss, and Whiskey Pete are true closers who will find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal, compromising their natural late finishes. This race shape — a sole front-runner controlling a sedate pace with a wall of hold-up horses unable to get far enough back — strongly favours Yafaarr to control and potentially win, or at minimum benefits the nearest prominent tracker Ceinture d'Orion, while genuine closers face a tactical lottery with a pace likely too modest to generate the late sectionals they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Yafaarr Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Yafaarr is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and set a comfortable tempo that becomes a test of stamina and resolution.
scenarios.body: Horgan dictates on a lone front-runner's terms, injecting just enough pace to keep rivals honest without burning Yafaarr's reserves, and the lack of any rival capable of going with him through the early stages means the race is run entirely to his rhythm. Hold-up horses face too modest a pace to generate the late acceleration they need on Good ground, leaving prominent and front-running profiles to dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Yafaarr's pace is just slow enough that a prominent runner can reel him in over the final two furlongs with a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: Ceinture d'Orion tracks Yafaarr throughout and, with David Nolan timing a move from the two-pole, uses a length or two of head start on the hold-up runners to collar the leader near the line. Always Blue, with the youngest legs in the race and a placed effort at 1m2f in her most recent start, could also press into contention from a handy early position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Exploit Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so restrained that even the hold-up horses, forced to race closer than usual, find themselves well-positioned to challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo compresses the field into a bunch by the final turn, negating the redistribution disadvantage and releasing closers into a genuine sprint finish where fresh legs count. Boubyan's strong recent form and multiple placed efforts on Good ground give it the best credentials among the hold-up contingent if the race develops into a dash, and Chesneys Charm's hold-up style from Jason Hart could also produce a finishing effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Yafaarr either races too freely early or fades abruptly in the straight, turning the race into a scramble.
scenarios.body: An overly bold or erratic front-running display by Yafaarr could cause the field to bunch chaotically in the straight with no clear leader, opening the door for any runner with tactical versatility to grab the prize. Adiada's hg:h (hood) suggests a degree of freshness or keenness management by Michael Dods, and a race in disarray could suit a horse travelling well within itself mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Yafaarr's front-running role is the fulcrum of the entire race — watch whether Cian Horgan sits comfortably or is asked to quicken early; if Yafaarr is allowed to bowl along uncontested, he becomes very hard to pass.

Ceinture d'Orion must secure second position cleanly at the start — if the hold-up horde pushes forward and crowds David Nolan out of the prominent spot, his entire race plan is compromised before the first bend.

Always Blue is the one hold-up runner in the field with a genuinely unexplored ceiling at 1m2f; Sean Bowen may elect to ride more positively than her style tag suggests given the likely slow pace, making her early position worth tracking.

Boubyan's hood (hg:p) and consecutive placed form on Good ground makes it statistically the most consistent closer in the race — but monitor whether Lewis Edmunds finds clear daylight in the straight given how many horses will be switching and weaving for the same late ground.

The weight of redistributed hold-up types (Cosmos Raj, Boubyan, Sweet Kiss, Whiskey Pete) means the straight at Redcar could become crowded and scrappy; any horse racing widest of all in the final two furlongs may get a cleaner run than those on the rail.

races.name: Market Cross Jewellers Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Raatea
runners_data.note: Veteran 9-year-old hold-up type who has shown recent placed form at 6f on Good (2nd and 3rd on similar going), but the sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 runs on similar ground is a significant concern; Tom Kiely-Marshall rides as a 5lb claimer and may offset the burden, but this horse needs the closers' scenario to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Raatea at least brings distance and going experience to the table and, rated 82 by us, shapes as a leading threat from stall 4 after 29 days off — though the trainer's recent 5% strike rate is a concern hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 5f on Good are striking but this race is over 6f — a trip she has not been asked to tackle in recent outings — and her hold-up style means she must wait on others to set up a race for her; David Nolan's experience is an asset and the T14 record of 2 wins from 15 is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Hover On The Wind has experience of today's distance and going, and he showed his best with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, though a pair of seventh-place finishes in his last two outings gives pause; carrying 138 lb from stall 7 on a quick eight-day turnaround adds to the query marks.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, boasting a strong record at 6f on Good (2 wins, 7 placed from 12 runs on similar going) and recent placed efforts at this distance; Jack Garritty knows the horse well and an uncontested lead on flat Redcar is precisely the scenario he thrives in — the tactical card is obvious and compelling.
runners_data.comment: Ingleby Archie landed a win three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, arriving here on a fresh 29-day break with his rating of 74 giving him every right to compete; the fifth last time out is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Sugar Baby
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up specialist with three wins and four places from 12 runs at 6f on Good ground, including a recent win at this trip; Billy Garritty's claim helps at the weights and this horse's course-and-distance profile is legitimate, though a truly honest pace is needed for her to land a blow from off it.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has since posted a seventh and an unplaced effort, leaving his form looking patchy; he has run over today's trip and going, draws stall one, and 135 lb is a stern enough burden for a gelding rated 70.

runners_data.name: The Caltonian
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old whose true running style is hold-up but the congestion of rear-placed horses in this field means he is unlikely to get that position naturally — his sim-going record of 0 wins from 5 at 6f on Good is also a red flag, and the style compromise compounds the concern; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a minor positive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, The Caltonian nevertheless rates considerably higher than his official mark suggests, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; fourth last time out — his best recent effort — and returning after just 15 days, he looks the one to beat from stall six carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old carries a strong recent form string (3-5-2-3-1-3 at 6f on Good), and Connor Beasley is adept at positioning horses just off the pace; his natural prominent role is exactly where he will travel in this race, and he represents the most credible threat to Ingleby Archie if the leader fades.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Mr Cool has placed in five of his last six starts but that sole win highlights the inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 133 lb from stall 11, and our rating of 72 suggests a shade of improvement on his official mark.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with four places on Good going but no win in that scenario, and the field's hold-up congestion means Fentiman will struggle to find his natural position; the hood (b) is noted and recent efforts at 5f rather than 6f suggest the trip extension is not a given — style compromise reduces confidence.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Applause posted a second last time out and a third three starts back, showing he can hit the frame, but he remains yet to win in his last five starts and a trainer running at just 5% over the past fortnight gives limited confidence from stall 2 off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Liverpool Star
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old lightly weighted at 129lbs, and Michael & David Easterby's runner has a 6f win on Good ground to his name; however, with true hold-up tendencies being squeezed by the field's density at the rear, Shay Farmer (5lb claim) may find himself further forward than ideal, diluting the closer's advantage.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Consistent placer — six places from recent runs at 6f on Good — but the 0-wins from 14 runs in similar conditions paints a picture of a horse that gets close without converting; forced further forward than his natural position by field congestion, his late run will be blunted, though his consistency makes him a danger to be on-side in any finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Taygar has shown consistency in placing but the string of near-misses is hard to ignore, and a ranking of ninth of eleven on our figures makes her difficult to fancy, despite having run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Showtime Mahomes
runners_data.note: Form at 6f on Standard (AW) rather than Good turf is a meaningful surface concern — sim-going record shows just 0 wins from 4 and 1 place on Good, which is thin evidence — and as a true hold-up type shuffled forward by redistribution, his path to victory involves racing out of his comfort zone on both counts.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in four of his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Showtime Mahomes is hard to fancy here, though he has experience of today's trip and conditions and returns on a reasonable 16-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Missmimi
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer with two wins and four places from 6 runs on Good at 5-6f, and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim keeps the weight manageable; she will likely sit second or third to Ingleby Archie and is well positioned to pounce if the leader weakens, though she needs to be sharp enough to repel Mr Cool at the same time.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of our assessments on a bare 60 rating, Missmimi is hard to fancy in this field, though she does offer a win three starts back and has experience over today's trip and conditions, and 17 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Ingleby Archie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jack Garritty can dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on Good ground at Redcar. The pace will be honest but not frantic — a lone leader rarely burns itself out, meaning the race is likely to be run at a measured tempo that keeps those in behind in a genuine race rather than a dawdle. Mr Cool and Missmimi will push forward from the prominent position, keeping some pressure on Ingleby Archie through the early and middle stages, but neither is likely to fire it up enough to unsettle the leader's rhythm. This race shape strongly favours hold-up types that can reel in a controlled pace over the final two furlongs — but critically, this field is heavily loaded with genuine hold-up horses that cannot all get their natural rearward position; The Caltonian, Spirit Of Applause, Liverpool Star, Taygar and Showtime Mahomes are all true hold-up types remapped to midfield, meaning the map overstates how far back they will travel — the horses most likely to secure their natural positions at the fore are Ingleby Archie, Mr Cool and Missmimi, and it is this prominent-to-front group that stands to benefit most if the pace is moderate and the field fans wide late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Archie Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie dictates an uncontested, sustainable gallop and the chasing pack cannot close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Garritty has a lead to himself, can control the fractions on flat Redcar, and Ingleby Archie's recent form (1-2-3 at 6f on Good) shows he thrives precisely in this scenario; a moderate tempo on Good ground means his stamina reserves are not drained and he has enough left to repel challenges. Mr Cool and Missmimi, racing prominently, are best placed to challenge but need him to come back to them, which is less likely if the pace is measured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough that Ingleby Archie ties late and the nearest chasers Mr Cool and Missmimi pick up the scraps.
scenarios.body: Mr Cool has a strong 6f record on Good ground (1-2-3 type form), and Connor Beasley is an experienced and astute handler of pace scenarios; if Ingleby Archie has done fractionally too much early, both Mr Cool and Missmimi hit their stride at the ideal moment. This shape suits horses who press the pace from second or third, and these two are natural inhabitants of that position unlike the redistributed horses behind them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is brisk enough that Ingleby Archie has used himself up and the field opens a gap for closers to burst through.
scenarios.body: Hover On The Wind, a genuine hold-up type with proven ability on Good going (two wins at 5f on Good recently), is best placed among the true hold-up brigade to take advantage, though the redistribution of so many runners to midfield means the late run is more congested than it appears on paper. Sugar Baby's course form and three wins at 6f on Good give her each-way claims, but this scenario requires a pace that simply may not materialise given the lone front-runner can dictate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the race crawls early, the entire field compresses at the two-furlong pole and it becomes a sprint for fitness and draw rather than tactics.
scenarios.body: In a bunch finish on flat Redcar, horses with the highest recent form figures and best current fitness benefit, and Hover On The Wind's recent back-to-back wins at 5f on Good give her a fitness edge; however, this scenario is the least likely given the presence of genuine prominent types who will ensure at least some forward pressure. Raatea and Spirit Of Applause are long shots if pace collapses completely and the field fans wide.

watchPoints.text: Ingleby Archie's unchallenged lead is the central tactical fact — if Garritty slots him into an uncontested rhythm in the first two furlongs, the race may already be won, and punters should watch whether any horse tries to take him on early.

The volume of redistributed hold-up horses (The Caltonian, Spirit Of Applause, Liverpool Star, Taygar, Showtime Mahomes) means the early-to-mid race pack will be denser than expected — watch for traffic problems and interference at around the 2f pole as these horses try to find runs simultaneously.

Hover On The Wind is stepping up from 5f to 6f for the first time in recent form — watch how she travels in the first half of the race, as a horse used to a sharper finish may find the longer straight at Redcar tests her stamina more than the market anticipates.

Mr Cool's trainer Charlie Johnston has a T14 strike rate of 7 wins from 40 runners — the volume and frequency of runners is high, suggesting a yard in form; Connor Beasley rides and the combination of in-form stable and experienced jockey on a horse with the right profile is worth monitoring in the market.

Going is confirmed Good for the 7:00 race and has remained stable throughout the card — no deterioration to factor in, meaning horses with strong Good-ground form figures (Ingleby Archie, Mr Cool, Missmimi) are operating on their optimal surface without adjustment needed.

races.name: Market Cross Jewellers Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: Has winning form at 6f and 7f on good ground and is the key pace influence here; her T14 record of 1/11 is modest but she is in a clear positional comfort zone, and with Stammers claiming, weight is aided — the slight STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she is technically mapped as prominent rather than a pure lead type, but in this field she will almost certainly hit the front.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out is a concern, but Farandaway boasts a lively recent record with a winner three starts back and another victory five starts back, and he brings distance and going experience plus a trim turnaround of 15 days to support his claims from stall 5 at 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Bonnie's Boy
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a poor recent run of 49-404 and no wins in similar going across his last six, Fentiman's 3lb claim helps but this profile needs a true searching gallop to land a blow and the current race shape does not encourage that.
runners_data.comment: Bonnie's Boy has run over today's trip and going and, rated 77 by us against an official mark of 72, he holds a clear edge on ratings; fourth three of his last five starts suggests consistency without a win, but that upside looks live here.

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Garritty partners a filly who has two wins on good ground and placings from a hold-up position, though she has raced exclusively at 5f in her recent history — stepping to 6f at Redcar is the key question; if she stays the extra furlong she could be the most dangerous late runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Rotokura Belle arrives here fit on a 21-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and her third two starts back shows she retains ability; the worry is that she has managed only one win in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Irish Nectar
runners_data.note: Runs in a hood and has posted zero wins or places on comparable going in recent starts, with a form string reading 904049; Herrington's T14 figure of 4/14 is solid but the horse's current trajectory is discouraging for a race with pace being controlled up front.
runners_data.comment: Irish Nectar has run over today's trip and going before and, drawn from stall ten carrying 135 lb, his speed rating of 82 makes him a stronger threat than his official mark of 70 suggests; the main concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Easterby's yard is in form (4/84 T14) and this horse has a strong good-ground profile with ten runs in similar conditions producing two wins and three places; McSweeney rides and the prominent style maps naturally to this race shape, making Marajito the most credible market rival to the pacesetter.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and representing a trainer woefully out of form at just 5% over the past fortnight, Marajito is hard to fancy at the weights, though she does bring distance and going experience and a second last time out at least keeps her honest.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Midgley's runner has placed twice on good ground over 6f and David Nolan provides top-level jockey quality, but Cairdeas is a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map due to the volume of closers in this field — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 signals the positional compromise, and winning from off the pace in a controlled race will be difficult.
runners_data.comment: Cairdeas arrives on the back of a fourth last time out and is yet to win in recent starts, though a second three starts back shows he can get involved; he has run over today's trip and going, but 132 lb from stall seven gives connections plenty to consider.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Bowen takes over on a three-year-old who won over 6f on good ground and has strong course-trip credentials (sim-going 9/14); the visor is noted, and while ability is there, this is a genuine rear-of-field operator whose chances depend on a searching pace that looks unlikely given Farandaway's uncontested role.
runners_data.comment: Come On Over has managed just one win in his last six starts, with consecutive fourths in his two most recent outings doing little to inspire confidence, and ranked eighth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff task; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Magistery
runners_data.note: Beasley partners Dods' three-year-old who is 45 days off a run and whose best form came on soft ground (one win on soft over 6f); good-ground form is limited (5/9 sim runs, no wins), and the horse is a natural hold-up type shunted forward on the map in a field crowded with closers.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of ten on our figures and with three poor efforts in her last three starts, Magistery is hard to fancy in the current context; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a win in her last five starts shows ability exists, but she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Men Of Honour
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old has posted 4-9969 recently and has zero wins on good or standard going across 11 comparable runs; Sullivan rides but the horse's form trend is deeply uninspiring and it sits at the bottom of the weights for a reason — a genuine hold-up runner with very limited current upside.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Men Of Honour nevertheless carries a rating of 76 here, ranking him second of ten, and he has run over today's trip and going; the concern is that his recent finishes offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Speeding Bullet
runners_data.note: Hart partners a five-year-old for Midgley whose recent form string of 2-0775 includes a placed run on good ground but also several weakening efforts; 25 days since last run is fine, but as another genuine closer redistributed to midfield, the race shape as it stands asks this horse to do too much against an untroubled front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Speeding Bullet at least has experience of today's distance and going in his favour, and 25 days off looks a reasonable freshener; the weight of 127 lb from stall 3 is the reality check for a gelding rated just 62 officially.

races.paceDynamic: Farandaway is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, she is expected to stride into an uncontested lead and control the fractions over this flat Redcar 6f. Marajito is the most likely horse to push up and share the early pace from a prominent position, but even her presence is unlikely to generate the kind of pressured gallop that would undermine a measured Farandaway lead. The bulk of the field — Cairdeas, Come On Over, Magistery, Men Of Honour and Speeding Bullet — are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for all of them to race from their natural position at the rear, meaning several will inevitably race closer than ideal and unlikely to secure a meaningful late run from off the pace. On good ground at a flat track where a controlled pace rewards those who travel smoothly just off the leader, this race shape strongly favours front-running or prominent-racing profiles who can control their own destiny rather than closers forced to make up ground against a potentially unchallenged pacesetter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farandaway Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Farandaway leads unopposed and sets a comfortable, metronomic gallop that the closers can never reel in.
scenarios.body: Farandaway dictates every yard, conserving energy through the first half of the race before Stammers asks her to stretch clear in the final two furlongs; on good ground at flat Redcar this is a near-ideal setup for a front-runner with her profile of recent wins at this trip and surface. Marajito, travelling prominently, is best placed to pick up the pieces if Farandaway ties up late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Marajito pushes up to track Farandaway closely and the two share a pressured but not frantic gallop that tests both.
scenarios.body: Farandaway is pressed enough to soften, and the race becomes a battle of stamina between the front two in the final furlong; Marajito's good-ground form and Easterby's recent record give her solid claims here. Rotokura Belle, who has shown she can produce a late thrust from a handy position, is the most likely beneficiary if both leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and Farandaway or Marajito overcook the fractions, leaving the race open to runners finishing strongly.
scenarios.body: Come On Over, who has strong good-ground credentials and a recent win over course-relevant trips, and Cairdeas, placed twice on good going, are the most likely to benefit from a true end-to-end gallop; however, both are flagged as redistributed hold-up types likely to race closer than ideal, which tempers confidence in a clean late run. Rotokura Belle, with two wins on good ground, also comes into the picture if she gets a clear passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble No Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down tactically with horses bunching and no clear rhythm established, creating a messy, compressed finish.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic race with no clean pace shape, value can emerge from horses with high positional flexibility, but most of this field are either genuine front-runners or true hold-up types forced out of role; Bonnie's Boy and Men Of Honour lack the recent form to capitalise convincingly. This is the least likely scenario given Farandaway's clear pace advantage and the straightforward flat Redcar track.

watchPoints.text: Farandaway's early stride — if she jumps cleanly and is allowed to bowl along unchallenged by the first furlong marker, the race is almost certainly hers to lose and every hold-up horse can be mentally discounted.

Marajito must be tracked in the early stages: if McSweeney pushes up to sit second and applies any pressure to Farandaway, the scenario shifts from a solo front-runner scenario to a genuine stamina test that opens the door for Rotokura Belle.

Rotokura Belle's sectionals around the 3f pole — she has raced exclusively at 5f recently, and if she begins to close between the 3f and 2f marks she is staying the trip; if she is still flat-footed at that stage the extra furlong has found her out.

Come On Over and Cairdeas are both flagged as hold-up horses racing out of position — watch where Bowen and Nolan actually place their mounts in the first furlong; if either ends up mid-pack or further back than the map shows, the redistribution has played out and their winning chance is sharply reduced.

Magistery's 45-day layoff means fitness is a mild concern — Beasley will likely be conservative early, and if the horse is seen getting outpaced before halfway, Dods' runner can be safely dismissed from any late-finish calculations.

races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Macedonian
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has shown modest recent form including a ninth from 20 runs ago; visor worn, Good-going record is weak (one place from six similar-ground runs) and dropping back from seven to six furlongs after a string of mid-field efforts suggests a marginal profile here.
runners_data.comment: Macedonian rates highest among today's twenty runners on our figures and carries fitness into this having shaped with promise when second last time out, giving him a strong profile at the weights despite the winless run in recent starts — the main risk is that his form either side of that placed effort has been well below par.

runners_data.name: Multaneighttothree
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner attempting to lead from gate to wire just two days after its last run, which is an unusual quick turnaround; connections with Grant Tuer clearly feel the horse is well, but the brevity of recovery and a form string suggesting no recent wins demands caution on whether it can sustain the gallop.

runners_data.name: Lindoro
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a blinkered headgear flag and a concerning finishing pattern noted; 62 days off the track is a significant absence, and a record of just three placed runs from five Good-ground starts without a win makes this a difficult horse to trust in a 20-runner competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Lindoro has run over today's trip and going before, but he arrives winless in his last five starts and his recent form makes for grim reading, with three unplaced efforts on the bounce; the 62-day break is a concern, though 135 lb from stall 15 gives connections something to work with.

runners_data.name: Stormy Pearl
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with an excellent Good-ground profile — 12 runs on similar going producing one win and four places — and consistent recent form figures of 3-3-4-3-5 over this exact six-furlong trip; Rhys Elliott takes the 5lb claim and the horse clearly handles Redcar's conditions.
runners_data.comment: Stormy Pearl arrives here fresh enough after 24 days off and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a third last time out highlighting her consistency; yet to score in recent starts is the flag to note, and 133 lb from stall 17 could test her.

runners_data.name: Heathers Feather
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type whose career has been run almost entirely at seven furlongs or beyond on Tapeta or Soft; just one of five similar-ground runs has produced a place, and the step down to six furlongs on Good turf represents a significant profile mismatch.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 17th of 20 on our figures, Heathers Feather returns just three days after finishing seventh, and his recent string of mid-to-rear finishes makes him very difficult to fancy, despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Strong profile for this contest — a six-furlong Good-ground winner from recent form and seven runs on similar going producing one win and one place; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps on a low weight, and the horse's tactical style suits a strongly-run six-furlong handicap.
runners_data.comment: Night Emperor won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but he carries 132 lb from stall 2 and his recent record shows only that single win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old from Tim Easterby's powerful yard who has posted placed runs in 11 of 15 similar-going starts and won over seven furlongs on Soft; dropping back to six here is a slight concern, but the yard is operating at a high strike rate and Jake Dickson's claim adds value.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out hints at a filly coming back to form, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but a struggling trainer at just 5% over the past fortnight is a concern, and 131 lb is a stiff enough burden from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Little Beck Annie
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won over this exact course, distance and going last time out at Good, which is a compelling recent form reference; 57 days since that run is worth noting but trainer Peter Niven also runs Hurstwood today, suggesting stable confidence is spread across the yard's string.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has struggled either side of that success, and 57 days off adds a fitness question; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 130 lb from stall 7, and a rating of 54 gives her a small edge over her official mark.

runners_data.name: Drish Samphire
runners_data.note: Won over six furlongs on Good ground and holds a decent course profile, but this horse's natural hold-up style means it has been pushed into the midfield map — in a 20-runner field with this many genuine backmarkers, it is unlikely to secure a prominent early position and its style-fit score of 0.92 reflects that positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Drish Samphire comes here on the back of a win fifteen days ago, and with experience of today's trip and going she arrives in solid nick, her recent victory the key reason she gets the nod despite a modest run of results before it.

runners_data.name: Fair Isle Sioux
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has run exclusively at seven furlongs or further in recent starts and whose best form on Good ground has been modest (no wins, no places from four similar-going runs); the drop to six furlongs on flat Redcar turf is a new question the form doesn't yet answer.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Fair Isle Sioux makes little appeal here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns after a 37-day break with conditions at least familiar.

runners_data.name: South Shore Island
runners_data.note: Capable prominent runner with two Good-ground placed runs from three recent starts over this trip; a Molly Keegan-Price 7lb claim is notable, and the horse has placed at six furlongs on Good going, making it a legitimate prominent-style contender in a field where that position is genuinely contested.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, South Shore Island does boast a second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, yet carrying 128 lb from stall 11 while rated just 48 officially leaves him with plenty to find against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Ellie's de Vega
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from Philip Kirby's yard with four placed efforts from 13 similar-going starts and a consistent record of prominent positions; blinkers are worn, and two days longer than stablemate Indy's Angel since last run means she is fractionally fresher, making her the more credible of the two Kirby runners on pace grounds.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last two starts, Ellie's de Vega arrives fresh on 14 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating has him ranked second among 20 rivals — the concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a genuine win and five places from 13 Good-ground starts, giving her the strongest recent form among the redistibuted hold-up horses; her natural style is rear-of-field, and in a 20-strong crowd she is likely to be further back than ideal, though the style-fit score of 0.93 is the highest among those displaced.
runners_data.comment: Battenburg Belle has run over today's trip and going, and her back-to-back thirds show consistent recent form, though a single win in her last six starts and 127 lb from stall 19 are the checks that keep her a midfield proposition.

runners_data.name: Mrs Trump
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer whose recent form figures are 7-6-8-7-6 — consistent, but consistently out of the frame; Paul Midgley's yard has placed two runners in the last 15 days and the mare handles Good ground, but the pattern of recent finishes makes it hard to build a case, and she will be further back than ideal in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Mrs Trump does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 15 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh; however, 126 lb and a rating of 46 make it hard to see her troubling the principals from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's second string, a hold-up type with three Good-ground placed runs from 15 similar outings; natural trailing style means she is displaced into midfield on the race map, and in a big field on a flat straight track, finding clear running from the rear will be the key challenge for Lewis Edmunds.
runners_data.comment: Indy's Angel showed promise when third last time out and second three starts back, but has been winless in her last six starts and ranked 14 of 20, she faces a stiff task from stall one despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who has posted six finishes all between fourth and seventh from 12 Good-ground starts — consistent but limited; Peter Niven's yard also runs Little Beck Annie and neither horse is likely to be favoured by a pace scenario that sees the field spread out, with Hurstwood's age and flat recent curve working against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Hurstwood at least brings experience of today's trip and going, and a return after 15 days suggests he arrives fresh; however, carrying 126 lb from stall 20 and rated 45 officially, he looks to have plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who wears a hood and has one win and one place from eight Good-ground starts; her true rear-of-field style is compressed into the midfield section of this map, and her form in 6-furlong Good-ground races (four runs, no wins) does not inspire confidence even if she gets a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent starts, Rinky Tinky Tinky faces a stiff ask from stall 14 carrying 126 lb, and ranked 15 of 20 on our figures; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 22-day freshener, are slim consolations.

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up performer with two places from ten Good-ground runs and a form string that includes no finish better than third in recent outings; pushed into the midfield section of the map by field size, and Andrew Elliott's booking on a horse with limited expectations looks like a routine ride rather than a significant stable signal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 16th of 20 on our figures, Ziva's Star faces a stiff ask from stall 16 carrying 126 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Wine
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has raced exclusively at five furlongs on Tapeta or Good and faces a first attempt at six furlongs on turf; Michael Dods also saddles Macedonian today, suggesting this is likely a second-string entry, and the step up in distance combined with the style-fit displacement (0.93) makes the profile difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 18th of 20 on our figures, Sparkling Wine faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and an unplaced effort last time out leaves connections with little to build on despite a 28-day freshener.

runners_data.name: Lady Grey
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old from Tim Easterby's yard with just three career starts, all on Good ground but over 5-7 furlongs; her form of 4-8-7 offers little encouragement and Duran Fentiman's booking on a horse with no placed runs suggests this is an educational outing in a big, competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lady Grey faces a stiff task here; a struggling trainer at 5% over the past fortnight offers little encouragement, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 24-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Multaneighttothree and Ellie's de Vega are the two confirmed front-runners in a 20-runner field, and with both likely to press for the early lead, the race will be run at an honest, competitive gallop from the outset on Good ground at Redcar's flat, straight six furlongs. The duo will engage from the gates and set a tempo that should stretch the field early, creating a race shape where those positioned in the first half-dozen lengths will be best placed to pounce inside the final two furlongs. Lope Y Linda is the most credible prominent type able to travel in their slipstream, while Fair Isle Sioux and South Shore Island may also secure early positions ahead of the compressed midfield. This race shape, with genuine pace but not a suicidal gallop, favours hold-up horses that can be close enough to the pace to benefit from the honest tempo — specifically progressive types with Good-ground form who can sustain their run from midfield; note however that the field contains far more natural hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear, and Drish Samphire, Battenburg Belle, Sparkling Wine, Indy's Angel, Mrs Trump, Hurstwood, Rinky Tinky Tinky, Ziva's Star and Lady Grey are all redistibuted into midfield — of these, Battenburg Belle and Drish Samphire are most likely to find positions closest to their natural style given their stronger recent profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Multaneighttothree and Ellie's de Vega set a genuine gallop that runs the stuffing out of early leaders, the closers who can be positioned mid-division with cover will be best served.
scenarios.body: The honest pace on flat Redcar ground creates a strong enough tempo that the front pair tire in the final furlong, handing the advantage to horses travelling well in fifth to tenth early on; Night Emperor's Good-ground win and Stormy Pearl's consistent placing record at this course and trip make them compelling beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves competitive but not truly gruelling, those racing in the top four or five positions will conserve enough energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: Lope Y Linda, tracking the two leaders with Tim Easterby's patient placing behind a big field, is ideally positioned to pounce as the pace-setters fade; South Shore Island and Fair Isle Sioux, both capable of prominent racing on Good ground, can also sustain their efforts to the line on this flat track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runners Brave It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders — most likely Ellie's de Vega, who has strong recent placed form and a Good-ground profile — is allowed to dominate without serious pressure, they could prove difficult to peg back over six furlongs.
scenarios.body: Redcar's straight six can reward a horse that gets a good break and settles into a rhythm, and Ellie's de Vega's repeated placed runs at 5-6 furlongs on Good ground suggest she handles the conditions well enough to make the most of any tactical advantage; Multaneighttothree running two days after its last start raises slight freshness questions, making Ellie's de Vega the more likely sole pace-setter if Multaneighttothree fades early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draw, Backmarkers
scenarios.trigger: If the large 20-runner field causes early crowding, gaps appear wide, and the two front-runners cancel each other out dramatically, a big-field lottery scenario opens up.
scenarios.body: In this scenario, the race fragments and a horse from the rear of the field threads through a collapsing contest, though this is materially discounted because most of the true hold-up types in this field are redistributed horses unlikely to find their natural position; Battenburg Belle, with a genuine win and multiple places on Good ground at this trip and the highest style-fit score among the redistributed horses, is the most credible lottery beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Multaneighttothree ran just two days ago — watch how quickly it begins to tire in the final two furlongs as the pace it sets potentially takes its toll, as early leader collapse is the key race-shape trigger for hold-up horses to strike.

With 20 runners over six furlongs on a straight track, monitor the draw and early positioning closely — Ellie's de Vega and Multaneighttothree may clip heels or hamper prominent types like Lope Y Linda if the field bunches on the stands side in the opening furlong.
